# CI test dependencies for Raven — pinned, and shared by ci.yml and coverage.yml.
#
# Why this file exists at all, in two parts:
#
# 1. Why a hand-picked list rather than `pdm install`: raven's full dependency tree pulls in
#    torch+torchvision (multi-GB) and the Python-version-pinned kokoro/misaki TTS stack, none of
#    which the test suite needs, and a matrix would install it once per entry on every push. The
#    workflows install this list, then `pip install -e . --no-deps` so the rest is never resolved.
#
# 2. Why pinned: unpinned, every name here resolved to whatever PyPI served that morning, so the
#    tested environment drifted without any commit saying so. On 2026-08-02 trafilatura 2.2.0
#    shipped and turned main red on all three platforms, and the cost was a round of "what did I
#    just break?" attached to an unrelated commit. Red CI should mean *your* commit broke
#    something. Dependabot bumps these (see .github/dependabot.yml), so a breaking release still
#    arrives — as a reviewable PR whose CI is red, rather than silently on main.
#
# Why one file rather than a list in each workflow: they had already drifted. `qoi` was in ci.yml
# but not coverage.yml, so the three qoi round-trip tests `importorskip`ed away in the coverage
# job alone — 1606 tests in CI against 1603 in Coverage, with nothing reporting the gap.
#
# Scope, stated so the next reader knows it is deliberate: only *direct* dependencies are pinned.
# The transitive closure still floats, so a broken release one level down can still surprise us.
# Pinning the full closure would be a ~50-line lockfile for a deliberately minimal test subset,
# and Dependabot churn to match. Revisit if a transitive break actually happens.
#
# torch and torchvision are NOT here: they install from PyTorch's own CPU wheel index, which needs
# an --index-url that would apply to this whole file. They are pinned inline in both workflows
# instead. Dependabot cannot track them there, so they need a manual bump now and then.
#
# Versions are the ones that passed on main at 1cc20a2 (CI run 30772151270).

bibtexparser==2.0.0b9
# The GUI toolkit. Here so that the tests which drive a DPG context — `raven/common/gui/tests/` and
# `raven/librarian/tests/test_chat_controller.py` — actually run, instead of `importorskip`-ing away on
# every CI run and reporting a skip that looks like a pass. Tests that *map a window* stay out regardless:
# they carry the `gui` marker and need `--run-gui`, which CI does not pass.
dearpygui==2.3.1
feedparser==6.0.14
# Needed *because* of `dearpygui` above, not on its own account: the GUI tests import
# `raven.common.gui.utils`, which reaches the vendored `DearPyGui_Markdown`, whose parser imports this.
mistletoe==1.6.0
# Also needed because of the GUI tests: `raven.common.gui.qroverlay` imports it to build the exhibit
# overlay's QR matrix, and `test_qroverlay.py` exercises that without a window.
segno==1.6.6
simpleeval==1.0.7  # librarian.llmtools, the `calculate` tool; `test_llmtools.py` exercises it
filelock==3.32.3  # common.datastorelock; keeps two frontends off one chat datastore
# `librarian.gguftokenizer` builds a tokenizer out of a GGUF. Its tests write a small one and read it back,
# so they need the pair — and that is the point of having them: it turns a construction verified by hand
# against one backend into one the suite checks on every push.
gguf==0.19.0
tokenizers==0.23.1
odfpy==1.4.1
Pillow==12.3.0
# Imported at module level by the adopted `file_dialog`, so `raven/vendor/file_dialog/tests/` needs it to
# collect at all — the tests themselves are pure-function and touch nothing psutil provides.
psutil==7.2.2
pypdf==6.16.1
pytest==9.1.1
pytest-cov==7.1.0
python-docx==1.2.0
python-pptx==1.0.2
PyYAML==6.0.3
qoi==0.7.2
requests==2.34.2
sseclient-py==1.9.0  # llmclient's SSE transport; needed since test_llmclient/test_scaffold started running here
tqdm==4.70.0
trafilatura==2.2.0
unpythonic==2.4.0
wosfile==0.7.0

# numpy 2.5.0 raised its floor to Python 3.12 (2.4.6 is >=3.11), so the matrix legitimately
# resolves two versions and pip is doing the right thing. Pinning one flat would break the 3.11
# entry; these markers reproduce what each entry already installs. Worth keeping rather than
# collapsing — it means the suite runs against both numpy majors.
numpy==2.4.6 ; python_version < "3.12"
numpy==2.5.2 ; python_version >= "3.12"
